cost threshold for parallelism

questions.q: In SQL Server, what does a Page Life Expectancy value persistently under 300 seconds on an OLTP workload indicate?

questions.explain: Partition pruning only activates when the WHERE clause filters on the partition key with a constant or stable expression — not a non-deterministic function — so queries that don't do this scan every partition.
options: The table must have more than ten million rows.
The query must use OFFSET-FETCH pagination.
The query's WHERE clause must filter on the partition key using a constant or stable expression (not a non-deterministic function).
The partition scheme must map each partition to a different filegroup.
questions.q: When does partition pruning actually take effect for a partitioned table?

questions.explain: Dropping a partition is a metadata-only operation — it completes instantly regardless of row count — which makes rolling-retention archiving trivially fast compared to batch deletes.
options: Because it is a metadata-only operation that completes instantly regardless of how many rows the partition contains.
Because it runs in parallel across all CPU cores while a DELETE is single-threaded.
Because DROP PARTITION releases buffer pool memory immediately.
Because TRUNCATE TABLE cannot be used on partitioned tables.
questions.q: Why is dropping a partition so much faster than deleting the same rows from a rolling-window retention table?

questions.explain: Async secondaries return data that's seconds or minutes behind the primary — fine for dashboards, but a user writing and then immediately reading back needs read-your-writes consistency, typically by routing those reads to the primary.
options: Queries on secondaries cannot use indexes and always scan.
ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly routing requires rewriting the application in .NET.
Asynchronous secondaries return slightly stale data, so read-your-writes scenarios need routing back to the primary.
Secondaries cannot serve reports while redo is running.
questions.q: What is the read-your-writes consistency challenge with asynchronous read replicas?

questions.explain: Workload isolation separates OLTP from analytics so they don't contend for CPU, I/O, buffer pool, and locks; SQL Server's Resource Governor implements this natively by classifying connections into workload groups with CPU/memory limits.
options: Resource Governor in SQL Server
The AG listener with ApplicationIntent routing
